character_facts: Aghnar is alive after decapitation by relying on machine attachment.
Honorata is the mysterious savior who helps Aghnar return to the Metabunker.
Honorata claims agency over Oda's restored body by reincarnating herself within it.
Oda is restored to life and becomes pregnant after the Shabda-Oud procedure.
Aghnar and Oda had previously agreed their child should not become a Metabaron.
The unborn child is male and becomes the focus of a future father-son conflict.
Honorata intends to raise her son to be capable of killing Aghnar.
characters_present: the unborn son of Aghnar and Oda
continuity_links: This page explicitly recaps events from earlier chapters before the main story continues.
It establishes the immediate backstory for a new stage of the Metabaron lineage centered on Aghnar, Oda, Honorata, and their son.
dialogue_meaning: The page is a prose recap summarizing prior events rather than scene dialogue.
Honorata explains how she survived and manipulated time on Okhar using Shabda-Oud powers.
Aghnar states his prior pact with Oda that their child should not become a Metabaron.
The recap frames the conflict as Honorata vowing to raise the son as a champion while Aghnar vows to return and kill him, reaffirming the clan's violent tradition.
lore_facts: The Shabda-Oud possess powers that can accelerate time and a psycho-surgical science capable of restoring someone to life.
Honorata had a 'heart-bomb' that could be replaced by expert robots after time acceleration on Okhar.
A specially built vessel can withstand the nuclear disintegration of a planet.
Time can pass at radically different rates for different parties in this setting.
Reincarnation or spirit transfer into another body is presented as possible.
A decapitated body can be kept alive by attaching it to a machine.
Metabaron tradition includes father-son lethal challenge as a recognized warrior custom.
plot_events: Aghnar leaves the Magon tribe and returns to the Metabunker through the intervention of a mysterious savior.

The savior is identified as Honorata, who explains that she used Shabda-Oud powers on Okhar to accelerate time so expert robots could replace her heart-bomb and build a vessel able to survive a planetary nuclear destruction.
Because of the altered time flow, about twenty years pass for Honorata on Okhar while only minutes pass for Othon and Aghnar in space.
Honorata offers to restore Oda to life using the psycho-surgical science of the Shabda-Oud, and Aghnar agrees.
Aghnar warns that he and Oda had agreed their child must not become a Metabaron.
The operation succeeds, Oda becomes pregnant, and the unborn child is identified as a boy.
During the pregnancy, Oda's attitude changes and she urges Aghnar not to miss the chance to make their son the greatest warrior in the universe.
It is revealed that Honorata has reincarnated herself inside Oda's body.
Aghnar realizes the truth and a mental struggle erupts between him and Honorata/Oda, with the baby taking the mother's side.
A laser shot suddenly blows off Aghnar's head.
Aghnar instructs Honorata to attach his decapitated body to a machine so he can continue living, because he wanted only to destroy her spirit.
Aghnar leaves after warning that he will return to challenge his son in a duel and destroy him.
Honorata accepts this as a renewal of Metabaron traditions and vows to raise her son into a warrior capable of killing his father.
uncertainties: The left-side painted figure and the five portrait medallions are not labeled on this page, so their exact identities are uncertain from this image alone.
